questions.q: Why is subledger-to-GL reconciliation especially important at month-end close?
options: If a subledger's period total doesn't match the GL for the same account, the trial balance is wrong and the period can't close cleanly
It has no real impact on the close process
It is only relevant for tax reporting, not the close
GL_BALANCES is always identical to the subledgers by default, so this check is redundant
questions.explain: AP and AR summarize into the GL; a mismatch between subledger and GL totals means the books don't tie out, blocking a clean period close.

questions.q: What does `GL_BALANCES.ACTUAL_FLAG = 'A'` filter the query to?
options: Only actual balances, excluding budget or encumbrance balances also stored in GL_BALANCES
Only balances from the current period
questions.explain: GL_BALANCES stores actual, budget, and encumbrance balances together; ACTUAL_FLAG = 'A' isolates the actual ones for a true financial comparison.

questions.q: In the AP-to-GL reconciliation query, what two columns are both subledger and GL totals grouped/joined by?
questions.explain: Both CTEs aggregate by period_name and code_combination_id, since reconciliation must compare the same account in the same period.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's reconciliation pattern (LEFT OUTER JOIN + NVL + difference <> 0) does this lesson's AP-to-GL query directly reuse?
questions.explain: The LEFT OUTER JOIN + NVL-guard + difference <> 0 structure is the exact reconciliation pattern introduced in Lesson 21, reapplied here at the subledger-to-GL level.

questions.q: What does AP_INVOICE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL.DIST_CODE_COMBINATION_ID represent in this reconciliation?
options: The specific chart-of-accounts combination (account) that an invoice distribution line is charged to
questions.explain: DIST_CODE_COMBINATION_ID identifies which GL account combination an AP distribution line hits, which is what gets matched against GL_CODE_COMBINATIONS/GL_BALANCES.
